key_insight: A SCAPS-1D plus machine-learning workflow can rapidly rank multilayer perovskite solar cell stacks and pinpoint the most influential layer descriptors for efficiency.
engineering_relevance: The study provides a practical design rule for optimizing ETL, absorber, and HTL combinations to accelerate discovery of high-efficiency, lead-free perovskite solar cells.
method: Trained an ML model on a representative subset to predict PCE for unexplored stacks.
Used Leave-One-Group-Out validation and SHAP to assess ranking quality and feature importance.
evidence_signal: The model showed reliable ranking under Leave-One-Group-Out cross-validation, and the best ML-suggested devices were confirmed by full SCAPS-1D simulations, including a top PCE of 28.85% for FTO/TiO2/Cs2AgBiBr6/NiO/Ag.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality and coverage of the simulated training set, so predictions may be less reliable when extrapolating to material systems outside the sampled design space.
paper_title: Multilayer Screening of Double and Conventional Perovskite Solar Cells Using SCAPS-1D and Machine Learning: Optimization of ETL, HTL, and Absorber for High-Efficiency Architectures
